executive_summary: The single most important connecting thread across today's content is the fragility of institutional safeguards and the systems societies rely on to contain high-stakes threats. The White House shooting incident — neutralized by Secret Service agents before casualties could mount — underscores how security infrastructure, when functioning, averts catastrophe, but also how quickly such threats can materialize without warning. This resonates directly with the Foreign Affairs newsletter on Ebola's lessons, which examines how public health institutions similarly serve as the critical barrier between manageable risk and systemic collapse, and how failures of preparation or response can prove catastrophic. Both stories, at their core, ask the same question: are our protective systems robust enough to handle the threats they were built to contain? That question carries urgent relevance at a moment when confidence in institutions — whether security agencies or global health bodies — is under sustained pressure worldwide.

items.headline: Making sense of an Alcaraz-less French Open
items.blurb: The French Open will not come down to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner. At least probably not, given that the tournament starts today at Roland Garros and Alcaraz is not in the draw because of a dreaded wrist injury. Without the two-time defending champion, there's a clear lane for his chief rival. The 24-year-old Sinner will complete the career Grand Slam if he takes care of business against a weakened field. The women's draw is a lot more open, with Iga Świątek and Aryna Sabalenka entering as roughly co-favorites.

items.headline: Knicks-Cavs is looking sweepy
items.blurb: The Knicks are on the verge of their first NBA Finals in 27 years after a 121-108 Game 3 victory in Cleveland, where home support and a certain famous couple didn't make the Cavs seem any less shell-shocked from their Game 1 collapse. Here's your regular reminder that no NBA team has ever blown a 3-0 lead.

breaking_digest.narrative: A gunman was shot and killed by Secret Service agents following a shooting incident near the White House, officials confirmed [1]. No further details on casualties or a motive were immediately available, and the incident remains under active investigation. Separately, the Cannes Film Festival concluded with the Norwegian film 'Fjord' claiming the prestigious Palme d'Or, the festival's top prize [2].
